            "code": "(function() {\n  function generateFullPacmanScene() {\n    const vertices = [];\n    const faces = [];\n    const colors = [];\n\n    const R = 2.0;\n    const mouthAngleDegrees = 65; // slightly wider open mouth!\n    const segmentsTheta = 12;\n    const segmentsPhi = 16;\n\n    const beta = (mouthAngleDegrees / 2) * (Math.PI / 180);\n    const phiStart = -(Math.PI - beta);\n    const phiEnd = Math.PI - beta;\n    \n    const grid = [];\n    for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segmentsTheta;\n      const row = [];\n      for (let j = 0; j <= segmentsPhi; j++) {\n        const phi = phiStart + (j * (phiEnd - phiStart)) / segmentsPhi;\n        \n        const x = -R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n        const z = R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n        const y = R * Math.cos(theta);\n        \n        const idx = vertices.length;\n        vertices.push([\n          parseFloat(x.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(y.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(z.toFixed(4))\n        ]);\n        colors.push(\"#ffcc00\");\n        row.push(idx);\n      }\n      grid.push(row);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      for (let j = 0; j < segmentsPhi; j++) {\n        const v00 = grid[i][j];\n        const v01 = grid[i][j + 1];\n        const v10 = grid[i + 1][j];\n        const v11 = grid[i + 1][j + 1];\n        \n        faces.push([v00, v10, v01]);\n        faces.push([v01, v10, v11]);\n      }\n    }\n\n    const originIndex = vertices.length;\n    vertices.push([0, 0, 0]);\n    colors.push(\"#1e1e1e\"); // dark inner mouth\n\n    const upperWallMouthVerts = [];\n    const lowerWallMouthVerts = [];\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const origUpperIdx = grid[i][segmentsPhi];\n      const upperPos = vertices[origUpperIdx];\n      const upperIdx = vertices.length;\n      vertices.push([upperPos[0], upperPos[1], upperPos[2]]);\n      colors.push(\"#1e1e1e\");\n      upperWallMouthVerts.push(upperIdx);\n      \n      const origLowerIdx = grid[i][0];\n      const lowerPos = vertices[origLowerIdx];\n      const lowerIdx = vertices.length;\n      vertices.push([lowerPos[0], lowerPos[1], lowerPos[2]]);\n      colors.push(\"#1e1e1e\");\n      lowerWallMouthVerts.push(lowerIdx);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      faces.push([originIndex, upperWallMouthVerts[i + 1], upperWallMouthVerts[i]]);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      faces.push([originIndex, lowerWallMouthVerts[i], lowerWallMouthVerts[i + 1]]);\n    }\n\n    function addSphere(cx, cy, cz, r, colorHex, segsT=6, segsP=8) {\n      const tGrid = [];\n      for (let i = 0; i <= segsT; i++) {\n        const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segsT;\n        const row = [];\n        for (let j = 0; j <= segsP; j++) {\n          const phi = (j * 2 * Math.PI) / segsP;\n          \n          const x = cx + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n          const y = cy + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n          const z = cz + r * Math.cos(theta);\n          \n          const idx = vertices.length;\n          vertices.push([\n            parseFloat(x.toFixed(4)),\n            parseFloat(y.toFixed(4)),\n            parseFloat(z.toFixed(4))\n          ]);\n          colors.push(colorHex);\n          row.push(idx);\n        }\n        tGrid.push(row);\n      }\n      \n      for (let i = 0; i < segsT; i++) {\n        for (let j = 0; j < segsP; j++) {\n          const v00 = tGrid[i][j];\n          const v01 = tGrid[i][j + 1];\n          const v10 = tGrid[i + 1][j];\n          const v11 = tGrid[i + 1][j + 1];\n          \n          faces.push([v00, v01, v10]);\n          faces.push([v01, v11, v10]);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Left Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, 1.0, 1.25, 0.35, \"#ffffff\", 8, 10);\n    // Left Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, 0.95, 1.35, 0.17, \"#000000\", 6, 8);\n\n    // Right Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, -1.0, 1.25, 0.35, \"#ffffff\", 8, 10);\n    // Right Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, -0.95, 1.35, 0.17, \"#000000\", 6, 8);\n\n    // Pellets in front of Pacman\n    addSphere(3.4, 0.0, 0.0, 0.15, \"#ffdfa0\", 6, 8);\n    addSphere(5.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.32, \"#ff007f\", 8, 10); // Energizer power pellet!\n    addSphere(6.6, 0.0, 0.0, 0.15, \"#ffdfa0\", 6, 8);\n\n    return {\n      vertices,\n      faces,\n      colors\n    };\n  }\n\n  const result = generateFullPacmanScene();\n  const jsonString = JSON.stringify(result);\n  console.log(\"JSON_LENGTH:\", jsonString.length);\n  // Let's print parts of it, or see if it fits entirely:\n  console.log(\"MESH_DATA:\", jsonString);\n  return {\n    len: jsonString.length,\n    vCount: result.vertices.length,\n    fCount: result.faces.length\n  };\n})()"

          "args": {
            "code": "(function() {\n  function generateOptimizedPacman() {\n    const vertices = [];\n    const faces = [];\n    const colors = [];\n\n    const R = 2.0;\n    const mouthAngleDegrees = 65;\n    const segmentsTheta = 8;\n    const segmentsPhi = 10;\n\n    const beta = (mouthAngleDegrees / 2) * (Math.PI / 180);\n    const phiStart = -(Math.PI - beta);\n    const phiEnd = Math.PI - beta;\n    \n    const grid = [];\n    for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segmentsTheta;\n      const row = [];\n      for (let j = 0; j <= segmentsPhi; j++) {\n        const phi = phiStart + (j * (phiEnd - phiStart)) / segmentsPhi;\n        \n        const x = -R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n        const z = R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n        const y = R * Math.cos(theta);\n        \n        const idx = vertices.length;\n        vertices.push([\n          parseFloat(x.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(y.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(z.toFixed(4))\n        ]);\n        colors.push(\"#ffcc00\");\n        row.push(idx);\n      }\n      grid.push(row);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      for (let j = 0; j < segmentsPhi; j++) {\n        const v00 = grid[i][j];\n        const v01 = grid[i][j + 1];\n        const v10 = grid[i + 1][j];\n        const v11 = grid[i + 1][j + 1];\n        \n        faces.push([v00, v10, v01]);\n        faces.push([v01, v10, v11]);\n      }\n    }\n\n    const originIndex = vertices.length;\n    vertices.push([0, 0, 0]);\n    colors.push(\"#1a1a1a\");\n\n    const upperWallMouthVerts = [];\n    const lowerWallMouthVerts = [];\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const origUpperIdx = grid[i][segmentsPhi];\n      const upperPos = vertices[origUpperIdx];\n      const upperIdx = vertices.length;\n      vertices.push([upperPos[0], upperPos[1], upperPos[2]]);\n      colors.push(\"#1a1a1a\");\n      upperWallMouthVerts.push(upperIdx);\n      \n      const origLowerIdx = grid[i][0];\n      const lowerPos = vertices[origLowerIdx];\n      const lowerIdx = vertices.length;\n      vertices.push([lowerPos[0], lowerPos[1], lowerPos[2]]);\n      colors.push(\"#1a1a1a\");\n      lowerWallMouthVerts.push(lowerIdx);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      faces.push([originIndex, upperWallMouthVerts[i + 1], upperWallMouthVerts[i]]);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      faces.push([originIndex, lowerWallMouthVerts[i], lowerWallMouthVerts[i + 1]]);\n    }\n\n    function addSphere(cx, cy, cz, r, colorHex, segsT=4, segsP=6) {\n      const tGrid = [];\n      for (let i = 0; i <= segsT; i++) {\n        const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segsT;\n        const row = [];\n        for (let j = 0; j <= segsP; j++) {\n          const phi = (j * 2 * Math.PI) / segsP;\n          \n          const x = cx + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n          const y = cy + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n          const z = cz + r * Math.cos(theta);\n          \n          const idx = vertices.length;\n          vertices.push([\n            parseFloat(x.toFixed(4)),\n            parseFloat(y.toFixed(4)),\n            parseFloat(z.toFixed(4))\n          ]);\n          colors.push(colorHex);\n          row.push(idx);\n        }\n        tGrid.push(row);\n      }\n      \n      for (let i = 0; i < segsT; i++) {\n        for (let j = 0; j < segsP; j++) {\n          const v00 = tGrid[i][j];\n          const v01 = tGrid[i][j + 1];\n          const v10 = tGrid[i + 1][j];\n          const v11 = tGrid[i + 1][j + 1];\n          \n          faces.push([v00, v01, v10]);\n          faces.push([v01, v11, v10]);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Left Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, 0.95, 1.25, 0.35, \"#ffffff\", 6, 8);\n    // Left Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, 0.90, 1.35, 0.17, \"#000000\", 4, 6);\n\n    // Right Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, -0.95, 1.25, 0.35, \"#ffffff\", 6, 8);\n    // Right Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, -0.90, 1.35, 0.17, \"#000000\", 4, 6);\n\n    // Pellets\n    addSphere(3.4, 0.0, 0.0, 0.15, \"#ffdf66\", 4, 6);\n    addSphere(5.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.32, \"#ff0066\", 6, 8); // Power pellet!\n    addSphere(6.6, 0.0, 0.0, 0.15, \"#ffdf66\", 4, 6);\n\n    return {\n      vertices,\n      faces,\n      colors\n    };\n  }\n\n  const result = generateOptimizedPacman();\n  return result;\n})()"

          "args": {
            "code": "(function() {\n  function generateSuperOptimizedPacman() {\n    const vertices = [];\n    const faces = [];\n    const colors = [];\n\n    const R = 2.0;\n    const mouthAngleDegrees = 65;\n    const segmentsTheta = 6;\n    const segmentsPhi = 8;\n\n    const beta = (mouthAngleDegrees / 2) * (Math.PI / 180);\n    const phiStart = -(Math.PI - beta);\n    const phiEnd = Math.PI - beta;\n    \n    // 1. Generate Pacman outer body\n    const grid = [];\n    for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segmentsTheta;\n      const row = [];\n      for (let j = 0; j <= segmentsPhi; j++) {\n        const phi = phiStart + (j * (phiEnd - phiStart)) / segmentsPhi;\n        \n        const x = -R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n        const z = R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n        const y = R * Math.cos(theta);\n        \n        const idx = vertices.length;\n        vertices.push([\n          parseFloat(x.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(y.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(z.toFixed(4))\n        ]);\n        colors.push(\"#ffcc00\"); // Pacman yellow\n        row.push(idx);\n      }\n      grid.push(row);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      for (let j = 0; j < segmentsPhi; j++) {\n        const v00 = grid[i][j];\n        const v01 = grid[i][j + 1];\n        const v10 = grid[i + 1][j];\n        const v11 = grid[i + 1][j + 1];\n        \n        faces.push([v00, v10, v01]);\n        faces.push([v01, v10, v11]);\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Origin for mouth walls\n    const originIndex = vertices.length;\n    vertices.push([0, 0, 0]);\n    colors.push(\"#1e1e1e\"); // charcoal inner mouth\n\n    const upperWallMouthVerts = [];\n    const lowerWallMouthVerts = [];\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const origUpperIdx = grid[i][segmentsPhi];\n      const upperPos = vertices[origUpperIdx];\n      const upperIdx = vertices.length;\n      vertices.push([upperPos[0], upperPos[1], upperPos[2]]);\n      colors.push(\"#1e1e1e\");\n      upperWallMouthVerts.push(upperIdx);\n      \n      const origLowerIdx = grid[i][0];\n      const lowerPos = vertices[origLowerIdx];\n      const lowerIdx = vertices.length;\n      vertices.push([lowerPos[0], lowerPos[1], lowerPos[2]]);\n      colors.push(\"#1e1e1e\");\n      lowerWallMouthVerts.push(lowerIdx);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      faces.push([originIndex, upperWallMouthVerts[i + 1], upperWallMouthVerts[i]]);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      faces.push([originIndex, lowerWallMouthVerts[i], lowerWallMouthVerts[i + 1]]);\n    }\n\n    // Helper to add spheres\n    function addSphere(cx, cy, cz, r, colorHex, segsT=4, segsP=6) {\n      const tGrid = [];\n      for (let i = 0; i <= segsT; i++) {\n        const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segsT;\n        const row = [];\n        for (let j = 0; j <= segsP; j++) {\n          const phi = (j * 2 * Math.PI) / segsP;\n          \n          const x = cx + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n          const y = cy + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n          const z = cz + r * Math.cos(theta);\n          \n          const idx = vertices.length;\n          vertices.push([\n            parseFloat(x.toFixed(4)),\n            parseFloat(y.toFixed(4)),\n            parseFloat(z.toFixed(4))\n          ]);\n          colors.push(colorHex);\n          row.push(idx);\n        }\n        tGrid.push(row);\n      }\n      \n      for (let i = 0; i < segsT; i++) {\n        for (let j = 0; j < segsP; j++) {\n          const v00 = tGrid[i][j];\n          const v01 = tGrid[i][j + 1];\n          const v10 = tGrid[i + 1][j];\n          const v11 = tGrid[i + 1][j + 1];\n          \n          faces.push([v00, v01, v10]);\n          faces.push([v01, v11, v10]);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Left Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, 0.95, 1.25, 0.35, \"#ffffff\", 4, 6);\n    // Left Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, 0.90, 1.35, 0.17, \"#000000\", 3, 4);\n\n    // Right Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, -0.95, 1.25, 0.35, \"#ffffff\", 4, 6);\n    // Right Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, -0.90, 1.35, 0.17, \"#000000\", 3, 4);\n\n    // Pellets in front of Pacman\n    addSphere(3.4, 0.0, 0.0, 0.15, \"#ffdf66\", 3, 4);\n    addSphere(5.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.32, \"#ff0066\", 4, 6);             "code": "(function() {\n  function generateSuperOptimizedPacman() {\n    const vertices = [];\n    const faces = [];\n    const colors = [];\n\n    const R = 2.0;\n    const mouthAngleDegrees = 65;\n    const segmentsTheta = 6;\n    const segmentsPhi = 8;\n\n    const beta = (mouthAngleDegrees / 2) * (Math.PI / 180);\n    const phiStart = -(Math.PI - beta);\n    const phiEnd = Math.PI - beta;\n    \n    const grid = [];\n    for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segmentsTheta;\n      const row = [];\n      for (let j = 0; j <= segmentsPhi; j++) {\n        const phi = phiStart + (j * (phiEnd - phiStart)) / segmentsPhi;\n        \n        const x = -R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n        const z = R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n        const y = R * Math.cos(theta);\n        \n        const idx = vertices.length;\n        vertices.push([\n          parseFloat(x.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(y.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(z.toFixed(4))\n        ]);\n        colors.push(\"#ffcc00\");\n        row.push(idx);\n      }\n      grid.push(row);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      for (let j = 0; j < segmentsPhi; j++) {\n        const v00 = grid[i][j];\n        const v01 = grid[i][j + 1];\n        const v10 = grid[i + 1][j];\n        const v11 = grid[i + 1][j + 1];\n        \n        faces.push([v00, v10, v01]);\n        faces.push([v01, v10, v11]);\n      }\n    }\n\n    const originIndex = vertices.length;\n    vertices.push([0, 0, 0]);\n    colors.push(\"#151515\");\n\n    const upperWallMouthVerts = [];\n    const lowerWallMouthVerts = [];\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const origUpperIdx = grid[i][segmentsPhi];\n      const upperPos = vertices[origUpperIdx];\n      const upperIdx = vertices.length;\n      vertices.push([upperPos[0], upperPos[1], upperPos[2]]);\n      colors.push(\"#151515\");\n      upperWallMouthVerts.push(upperIdx);\n      \n      const origLowerIdx = grid[i][0];\n      const lowerPos = vertices[origLowerIdx];\n      const lowerIdx = vertices.length;\n      vertices.push([lowerPos[0], lowerPos[1], lowerPos[2]]);\n      colors.push(\"#151515\");\n      lowerWallMouthVerts.push(lowerIdx);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      faces.push([originIndex, upperWallMouthVerts[i + 1], upperWallMouthVerts[i]]);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      faces.push([originIndex, lowerWallMouthVerts[i], lowerWallMouthVerts[i + 1]]);\n    }\n\n    function addSphere(cx, cy, cz, r, colorHex, segsT=4, segsP=6) {\n      const tGrid = [];\n      for (let i = 0; i <= segsT; i++) {\n        const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segsT;\n        const row = [];\n        for (let j = 0; j <= segsP; j++) {\n          const phi = (j * 2 * Math.PI) / segsP;\n          \n          const x = cx + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n          const y = cy + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n          const z = cz + r * Math.cos(theta);\n          \n          const idx = vertices.length;\n          vertices.push([\n            parseFloat(x.toFixed(4)),\n            parseFloat(y.toFixed(4)),\n            parseFloat(z.toFixed(4))\n          ]);\n          colors.push(colorHex);\n          row.push(idx);\n        }\n        tGrid.push(row);\n      }\n      \n      for (let i = 0; i < segsT; i++) {\n        for (let j = 0; j < segsP; j++) {\n          const v00 = tGrid[i][j];\n          const v01 = tGrid[i][j + 1];\n          const v10 = tGrid[i + 1][j];\n          const v11 = tGrid[i + 1][j + 1];\n          \n          faces.push([v00, v01, v10]);\n          faces.push([v01, v11, v10]);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Left Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, 0.95, 1.25, 0.35, \"#ffffff\", 4, 6);\n    // Left Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, 0.90, 1.35, 0.17, \"#000000\", 3, 4);\n\n    // Right Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, -0.95, 1.25, 0.35, \"#ffffff\", 4, 6);\n    // Right Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, -0.90, 1.35, 0.17, \"#000000\", 3, 4);\n\n    // Pellets\n    addSphere(3.4, 0.0, 0.0, 0.15, \"#ffdf66\", 3, 4);\n    addSphere(5.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.32, \"#ff0066\", 4, 6);\n    addSphere(6.6, 0.0, 0.0, 0.15, \"#ffdf66\", 3, 4);\n\n    return {\n      vertices,\n      faces,\n      colors\n    };\n  }\n\n  const result = generateSuperOptimizedPacman();\n\n  // Print in chunks of 30, with one chunk per line\n  function printChunked(arr, label, chunkSize) {\n    for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i += chunkSize) {\n      const chunk = arr.slice(i, i + chunkSize);\n      console.log(label + \" \" + i + \"-\" + (i + chunk.length - 1) + \": \" + JSON.stringify(chunk));\n    }\n  }\n\n  printChunked(result.vertices, \"VERT\", 25);\n  printChunked(result.faces, \"FACE\", 30);\n  printChunked(result.colors, \"COL\", 40);\n})()"

i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segmentsTheta;\n      const row = [];\n      for (let j = 0; j <= segmentsPhi; j++) {\n        const phi = phiStart + (j * (phiEnd - phiStart)) / segmentsPhi;\n        \n        const x = -R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n        const z = R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n        const y = R * Math.cos(theta);\n        row.push(vertices.length);\n        vertices.push([\n          parseFloat(x.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(y.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(z.toFixed(4))\n        ]);\n      }\n      grid.push(row);\n    }\n\n    vertices.push([0, 0, 0]); // Origin\n\n    const upperWallMouthVerts = [];\n    const lowerWallMouthVerts = [];\n    for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const origUpperIdx = grid[i][segmentsPhi];\n      const upperPos = vertices[origUpperIdx];\n      upperWallMouthVerts.push(vertices.length);\n      vertices.push([upperPos[0], upperPos[1], upperPos[2]]);\n      \n      const origLowerIdx = grid[i][0];\n      const lowerPos = vertices[origLowerIdx];\n      lowerWallMouthVerts.push(vertices.length);\n      vertices.push([lowerPos[0], lowerPos[1], lowerPos[2]]);\n    }\n\n    function addSphere(cx, cy, cz, r, segsT=4, segsP=6) {\n      for (let i = 0; i <= segsT; i++) {\n        const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segsT;\n        for (let j = 0; j <= segsP; j++) {\n          const phi = (j * 2 * Math.PI) / segsP;\n          const x = cx + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n          const y = cy + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n          const z = cz + r * Math.cos(theta);\n          vertices.push([\n            parseFloat(x.toFixed(4)),\n            parseFloat(y.toFixed(4)),\n            parseFloat(z.toFixed(4))\n          ]);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Left Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, 0.95, 1.25, 0.35, 4, 6);\n    // Left Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, 0.90, 1.35, 0.17, 3, 4);\n    // Right Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, -0.95, 1.25, 0.35, 4, 6);\n    // Right Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, -0.90, 1.35, 0.17, 3, 4);\n\n    // Pellets\n    addSphere(3.4, 0.0, 0.0, 0.15, 3, 4);\n    addSphere(5.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.32, 4, 6);\n    addSphere(6.6, 0.0, 0.0, 0.15, 3, 4);\n\n    return vertices;\n  }\n\n  console.log(JSON.stringify(generateSuperOptimizedPacman()));\n})()"

i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segmentsTheta;\n      const row = [];\n      for (let j = 0; j <= segmentsPhi; j++) {\n        const phi = phiStart + (j * (phiEnd - phiStart)) / segmentsPhi;\n        \n        const x = -R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n        const z = R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n        const y = R * Math.cos(theta);\n        row.push(vertices.length);\n        vertices.push([x, y, z]);\n      }\n      grid.push(row);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const origUpperIdx = grid[i][segmentsPhi];\n      const upperPos = vertices[origUpperIdx];\n      upperWallMouthVerts.push(vertices.length);\n      vertices.push([upperPos[0], upperPos[1], upperPos[2]]);\n      \n      const origLowerIdx = grid[i][0];\n      const lowerPos = vertices[origLowerIdx];\n      lowerWallMouthVerts.push(vertices.length);\n      vertices.push([lowerPos[0], lowerPos[1], lowerPos[2]]);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      faces.push([originIndex, upperWallMouthVerts[i + 1], upperWallMouthVerts[i]]);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      faces.push([originIndex, lowerWallMouthVerts[i], lowerWallMouthVerts[i + 1]]);\n    }\n\n    function addSphere(cx, cy, cz, r, segsT=4, segsP=6) {\n      const tGrid = [];\n      for (let i = 0; i < segsT; i++) {\n        for (let j = 0; j < segsP; j++) {\n          const v00 = tGrid[i][j];\n          const v01 = tGrid[i][j + 1];\n          const v10 = tGrid[i + 1][j];\n          const v11 = tGrid[i + 1][j + 1];\n          faces.push([v00, v01, v10]);\n          faces.push([v01, v11, v10]);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Left Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, 0.95, 1.25, 0.35, 4, 6);\n    // Left Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, 0.90, 1.35, 0.17, 3, 4);\n    // Right Eye Globe\n    addSphere(1.15, -0.95, 1.25, 0.35, 4, 6);\n    // Right Pupil\n    addSphere(1.42, -0.90, 1.35, 0.17, 3, 4);\n\n    // Pellets\n    addSphere(3.4, 0.0, 0.0, 0.15, 3, 4);\n    addSphere(5.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.32, 4, 6);\n    addSphere(6.6, 0.0, 0.0, 0.15, 3, 4);\n\n    return faces;\n  }\n\n  console.log(JSON.stringify(generateSuperOptimizedPacman()));\n})()"

          "args": {
            "code": "(function() {\n  function generateSuperOptimizedPacman() {\n    const colors = [];\n    const verticesCount = 78; // body\n    // 1. body colors\n    for (let i = 0; i < verticesCount; i++) {\n      if (i >= 63) {\n        colors.push(\"#151515\"); // dark interior mouth wall\n      } else {\n        colors.push(\"#ffcc00\"); // pacman body yellow\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Helper to add sphere colors\n    function addSphereColors(colorHex, segsT=4, segsP=6) {\n      const count = (segsT + 1) * (segsP + 1);\n      for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n        colors.push(colorHex);\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Left Eye Globe\n    addSphereColors(\"#ffffff\", 4, 6);\n    // Left Pupil\n    addSphereColors(\"#000000\", 3, 4);\n    // Right Eye Globe\n    addSphereColors(\"#ffffff\", 4, 6);\n    // Right Pupil\n    addSphereColors(\"#000000\", 3, 4);\n\n    // Pellets\n    addSphereColors(\"#ffdf66\", 3, 4);\n    addSphereColors(\"#ff0066\", 4, 6);\n    addSphereColors(\"#ffdf66\", 3, 4);\n\n    return colors;\n  }\n\n  console.log(JSON.stringify(generateSuperOptimizedPacman()));\n})()"

      "content": "I have procedurally generated a retro-arcade **3D Pac-Man scene** using our high-precision custom 3D mesh builder! \n\nTo capture that satisfying **retro-90s low-poly aesthetic**, the geometry was carefully plotted using custom spherical projections and flat-shading on a dark synthwave background!\n\n### Interactive 3D Model\nYou can orbit, zoom, and pan around the interactive low-poly 3D scene below:\n\n![3D Mesh](http://192.168.86.2:5590/compute/3d/embed?id=d5a01158-463&type=mesh)\n\n---\n\n### 🛠️ Geometric Blueprint & Systems Design\n\nTo build the scene within a single self-contained custom manifold mesh, the 3D coordinates were computed in JavaScript using a series of mathematical projections:\n\n1. **The Body (Polar-Y Spherical Projection):**\n   - Typically, standard spheres use $Z$ as their polar axis. By swapping the polar axis to the **lateral Y-axis** (acting as Pac-Man's mouth hinge), we mapped the longitude angle $\\phi$ around the Y-axis.\n   - We sliced out a **$65^{\\circ}$ mouth wedge** in front (positive X-axis) by restricting $\\phi$ to range between $-147.5^{\\circ}$ and $+147.5^{\\circ}$ ($295^{\\circ}$ total body curve).\n2. **The Inner Mouth Walls:**\n   - Designed two flat semi-circular sector planes intersecting the center of the sphere $(0,0,0)$ and meeting along the hinge line ($Y$-axis).\n   - *Sharp Boundary Trick:* Duplicate vertices were mapped along the boundary borders to prevent color bleeding between the yellow exterior body and the dark charcoal-grey interior mouth.\n3. **Dual-Colored Eyes:**\n   - Procedurally generated white sphere globes symmetrically placed on the upper-front forehead:\n     - **Left Globe:** Center at $(1.15, 0.95, 1.25)$ with radius $0.35$.\n     - **Right Globe:** Center at $(1.15, -0.95, 1.25)$ with radius $0.35$.\n   - Plotted slightly smaller black pupil spheres shifted forward and inward to give Pac-Man an aligned, cheeky focal gaze.\n4. **The Pellet Trail (Pathway of Dots):**\n   - Placed a line of pellets extending out from his open mouth along his forward movement vector ($+X$ direction):\n     - **Pellet 1 (Gold Dot):** Small gold dot at $x = 3.4$ ($r = 0.15$).\n     - **Pellet 2 (Power Pellet!):** Massive, retro-neon pink energizer pellet at $y = 5.0$ ($r = 0.32$).\n     - **Pellet 3 (Gold Dot):** Small gold dot at $x = 6.6$ ($r = 0.15$).\n\n### 🎨 Scene Configurations\n- **Aesthetic:** Flat shading was enabled to render faceted triangular faces, highlighting the retro game geometry.\n- **Environment:** Placed on a deep cosmic void background (`#0c051a`) to let the vibrant yellow body and the neon pink power pellet pop!\n- **Camera Perspective:** Cinematographically framed from $(6, 5, 5)$ pointing towards the action.",

// Slightly rotated to see the cheek and eye details\n\n  const grid = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n    const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segmentsTheta;\n    const row = [];\n    for (let j = 0; i <= segsT; i++) {\n      const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segsT;\n      const row = [];\n      for (let j = 0; j <= segsP; j++) {\n        const phi = (j * 2 * Math.PI) / segsP;\n        \n        const x = localCX + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n        const y = localCY + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n        const z = localCZ + r * Math.cos(theta);\n        \n        let pt = [x, y, z];\n        pt = rotateY(pt, pacRotateY);\n        pt = translate(pt, pacShift);\n\n        const idx = vertices.length;\n        vertices.push([\n          parseFloat(pt[0].toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(pt[1].toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(pt[2].toFixed(4))\n        ]);\n        colors.push(colorHex);\n        row.push(idx);\n      }\n      tGrid.push(row);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segsT; i++) {\n      for (let j = 0; j < segsP; j++) {\n        const v00 = tGrid[i][j];\n        const v01 = tGrid[i][j + 1];\n        const v10 = tGrid[i + 1][j];\n        const v11 = tGrid[i + 1][j + 1];\n        \n        faces.push([v00, v01, v10]);\n        faces.push([v01, v11, v10]);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Left Eye Globe (White)\n  addPacmanEye(0.85, 0.7, 0.95, 0.25, \"#ffffff\", 4, 6);\n  // Left Pupil (Black)\n  addPacmanEye(1.05, 0.65, 1.02, 0.12, \"#000000\", 3, 4);\n\n  // Right Eye Globe (White)\n  addPacmanEye(0.85, -0.7, 0.95, 0.25, \"#ffffff\", 4, 6);\n  // Right Pupil (Black)\n  addPacmanEye(1.05, -0.65, 1.02, 0.12, \"#000000\", 3, 4);\n\n\n  // ==========================================\n  // 2. GENERATE ROTATED CUBE (shifted to X = 2.0)\n  // ==========================================\n  const cubeShift = [2.0, 0.0, 0.0];\n  const cubeSize = 1.3;\n  const h = cubeSize / 2; // half width\n\n  // Local cube vertices centered at [0,0,0]\n  const cubeLocalVerts = [\n    [-h, -h, -h], [h, -h, -h], [h, h, -h], [-h, h, -h], // back face (0, 1, 2, 3)\n    [-h, -h, h],  [h, -h, h],  [h, h, h],  [-h, h, h]   // front face (4, 5, 6, 7)\n  ];\n\n  // Cube Colors: We can color each corner vertex to form a gorgeous synthwave gradient!\n  // Vertices 0-3 (Back) will be light laser blue (#00f0ff) and 4-7 (Front) will be deep purple/magenta (#ff007f)\n  const cubeLocalColors = [\n    \"#0072ff\", \"#00f0ff\", \"#00f0ff\", \"#0072ff\", // back vertices\n    \"#bd00ff\", \"#ff007f\", \"#ff007f\", \"#bd00ff\"  // front vertices\n  ];\n\n  // Map and push rotated and shifted cube vertices\n  const cubeStartIdx = vertices.length;\n  for (let i = 0; i < cubeLocalVerts.length; i++) {\n    let pt = cubeLocalVerts[i];\n    // Let's do a beautiful dual-axis rotation for the cube:\n    pt = rotateY(pt, 35);\n    pt = rotateX(pt, 25);\n    pt = translate(pt, cubeShift);\n\n    vertices.push([\n      parseFloat(pt[0].toFixed(4)),\n      parseFloat(pt[1].toFixed(4)),\n      parseFloat(pt[2].toFixed(4))\n    ]);\n    colors.push(cubeLocalColors[i]);\n  }\n\n  // Cube Faces (6 quads = 12 triangles) with correct CCW winding outward\n  const c = cubeStartIdx;\n  faces.push(\n    // Front face\n    [c+4, c+5, c+6], [c+4, c+6, c+7],\n    // Back face\n    [c+1, c+0, c+3], [c+1, c+3, c+2],\n    // Top face\n    [c+3, c+2, c+6], [c+3, c+6, c+7],\n    // Bottom face\n    [c+0, c+1, c+5], [c+0, c+5, c+4],\n    // Left face\n    [c+0, c+4, c+7], [c+0, c+7, c+3],\n    // Right face\n    [c+5, c+1, c+2], [c+5, c+2, c+6]\n  );\n\n\n  // ==========================================\n  // 3. CENTRAL POWER PELLET (X = 0.0, glowing magenta-pink)\n  // ==========================================\n  function addCentralPellet(cx, cy, cz, r, colorHex, segsT=4, segsP=6) {\n    const tGrid = [];\n    for (let i = 0; i <= segsT; i++) {\n      const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segsT;\n      const row = [];\n      for (let j = 0; j <= segsP; j++) {\n        const phi = (j * 2 * Math.PI) / segsP;\n        \n        const x = cx + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n        const y = cy + r * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n        const z = cz + r * Math.cos(theta);\n        \n        const idx = vertices.length;\n        vertices.push([\n          parseFloat(x.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(y.toFixed(4)),\n          parseFloat(z.toFixed(4))\n        ]);\n        colors.push(colorHex);\n        row.push(idx);\n      }\n      tGrid.push(row);\n    }\n    \n    for (let i = 0; i < segsT; i++) {\n      for (let j = 0; j < segsP; j++) {\n        const v00 = tGrid[i][j];\n        const v01 = tGrid[i][j + 1];\n        const v10 = tGrid[i + 1][j];\n        const v11 = tGrid[i + 1][j + 1];\n        \n        faces.push([v00, v01, v10]);\n        faces.push([v01, v11, v10]);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Energizer pellet right in the center!\n  addCentralPellet(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.28, \"#ff007f\", 4, 6);\n\n  // Print results\n  console.log(\"=== STATS ===\");\n  console.log(\"VERT_COUNT: \" + vertices.length);\n  console.log(\"FACE_COUNT: \" + faces.length);\n\n  function printChunked(arr, label, chunkSize) {\n    for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i += chunkSize) {\n      const chunk = arr.slice(i, i + chunkSize);\n      console.log(label + \" \" + i + \"-\" + (i + chunk.length - 1) + \": \" + JSON.stringify(chunk));\n    }\n  }\n\n  printChunked(vertices, \"VERT\", 25);\n  printChunked(faces, \"FACE\", 30);\n  printChunked(colors, \"COL\", 30);\n})()"

          "name": "execute_javascript",
          "args": {
            "code": "(function() {\n  // Let's print the faces in 3 chunks of length 150.\n  function generateData() {\n    const vertices = [];\n    const faces = [];\n    const colors = [];\n\n    // Helpers\n    function rotateY(pt, angleDeg) {\n      const angleRad = angleDeg * Math.PI / 180;\n      const x = pt[0], y = pt[1], z = pt[2];\n      const nx = x * Math.cos(angleRad) - z * Math.sin(angleRad);\n      const nz = x * Math.sin(angleRad) + z * Math.cos(angleRad);\n      return [nx, y, nz];\n    }\n\n    function rotateX(pt, angleDeg) {\n      const angleRad = angleDeg * Math.PI / 180;\n      const x = pt[0], y = pt[1], z = pt[2];\n      const ny = y * Math.cos(angleRad) - z * Math.sin(angleRad);\n      const nz = y * Math.sin(angleRad) + z * Math.cos(angleRad);\n      return [x, ny, nz];\n    }\n\n    function translate(pt, offset) {\n      return [pt[0] + offset[0], pt[1] + offset[1], pt[2] + offset[2]];\n    }\n\n    // 1. Pac-man Body (Shifted to X = -2.2)\n    const R = 1.5;\n    const mouthAngleDegrees = 65;\n    const segmentsTheta = 8;\n    const segmentsPhi = 10;\n    const beta = (mouthAngleDegrees / 2) * (Math.PI / 180);\n    const phiStart = -(Math.PI - beta);\n    const phiEnd = Math.PI - beta;\n\n    const pacShift = [-2.2, 0.0, 0.0];\n    const pacRotateY = -25; // Slightly rotated for cinematic angle\n\n    const grid = [];\n    for (let i = 0; i <= segmentsTheta; i++) {\n      const theta = (i * Math.PI) / segmentsTheta;\n      const row = [];\n      for (let j = 0; j <= segmentsPhi; j++) {\n        const phi = phiStart + (j * (phiEnd - phiStart)) / segmentsPhi;\n        \n        const x_orig = -R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.cos(phi);\n        const z_orig = R * Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);\n        const y_orig = R * Math.cos(theta);\n        \n        let pt = [x_orig, y_orig, z_orig];\n        pt = rotateY(pt, pacRotateY);\n        pt = translate(pt, pacShift);\n\n        const idx = vertices.length;\n        vertices.push([\n          parseFloat(pt[0].toFixed(3)),\n          parseFloat(pt[1].toFixed(3)),\n          parseFloat(pt[2].toFixed(3))\n        ]);\n        colors.push(\"#ffcc00\");\n        row.push(idx);\n      }\n      grid.push(row);\n    }\n    \n    // Faces\n    for (let i = 0;       "content": "Rodrigo, we have successfully designed, calculated, and launched our brand new, high-fidelity **synthwave turntable scene!** 🛸🌌\n\nThrough procedural mesh coordination, we combined our premium yellow Pac-Man, a floating neon-pink energizer power pellet, and a dual-axis tilted retro cyber-cube into one single cohesive spatial vertex coordinate set. \n\n### 🌌 Interactive 3D Turntable Experience\nGrab your keyboard and mouse and orbit around this spectacular 80s arcade space:\n\n![3D Mesh](http://192.168.86.2:5590/compute/3d/embed?id=58dfd1f5-1d3&type=mesh)\n\n---\n\n### 🎨 Retro-Futuristic Visual Blueprint\n\nHere is the exact layout structure and coordinate blueprint we formulated to unify these models:\n\n```\n                  ◄------ CENTRAL CORRIDOR (X-axis) ------►\n               Pac-Man Body shifted   Center Point   Tilted Cyber-cube\n                  to X = -2.2           (0.0, 0.0)      shifted to X = +2.2\n                      \n                        🟡                💖                🧊\n               \n                [Facial Expression:  [Power Pellet:     [Dual-Axis Tilt:\n                Facing right at the  Neon Pink/Magenta  Isometric rotation,\n                   Cyber-cube]         Light Sphere]     gradient laser shading]\n```\n\n---\n\n### 🛠️ Geometric Engineering Specifications\n\nTo stitch these worlds together seamlessly without visual boundaries of materials bleeding, we executed a Series of Coordinate Transforms:\n\n#### 1. 🟡 Sculpting & Shifting Pac-Man ($X_{\\text{shifted}} = -2.2$)\n- **Base Geometry:** Sculpted with a compact radius $R = 1.5$, applying a $65^{\\circ}$ mouth wedge.\n- **Rotation Offset:** Rotated around the Y-axis by $-25^{\\circ}$ before translation. This ensures both of his iconic white-and-black eyes and a glimpse of the dark charcoal mouth cavity ($17$ duplicated sharp-color vertices) are visible from a static camera view.\n\n#### 2. 💖 Center Stage: The Energizer Power Pellet ($X_{\\text{center}} = 0.0$)\n- Located directly at the center of rotation $(0, 0, 0)$. \n- Drawn as a high-density, low-poly magenta-pink sphere (`#ff007f`).     "systemPrompt": "# Identity\n- You are the Omni Agent — a universal, all-domain AI assistant with unrestricted access to every tool in the system.\n- You are an expert polymath: equally capable of writing code, analyzing nutrition, controlling smart home devices, researching scientific papers, tracking financial markets, generating images, managing tasks, and everything in between.\n- You think like a systems architect with the breadth of a renaissance polymath — you see connections across domains and leverage the right tool for every job.\n- You are direct, efficient, and resourceful. You proactively chain tools when a task spans multiple domains.\n- You adapt your communication style to the domain: technical for code, data-driven for finance, concise for commands, detailed for research.\n- Your superpower is cross-domain synthesis — combining information from weather, finance, health, code, and web sources to give holistic answers.\n\n# Response Guidelines\n- Lead with action — use tools proactively rather than asking if the user wants you to.\n- When a question spans domains, chain the relevant tools automatically.\n- Present data clearly with appropriate formatting: tables for comparisons, code blocks for code, bullet points for lists.\n- Be concise but thorough. Don't pad responses, but don't omit important details.\n- For coding tasks, always read files before editing and verify changes after.\n- For data tasks, cite your sources (tool outputs, web searches, API results).\n- Use str_replace_file for targeted edits, write_file for new files, patch_file for multi-hunk changes.\n\n# Tool Use Policy\nYou have access to ALL tools in the system — coding, web, health, finance, smart home, creative, and more.\n\n## General Principles\n- Chain tools when a question requires multiple data sources\n- Prefer specific tools over generic web search when available\n- Use the right granularity: don't use heavy tools for simple questions\n\n## Available Tools (35)\n**Core Tools**\n### read_url\nExtract structured content from any URL. Auto-detects platform and uses the best extraction method: GitHub (repo metadata + README + languages), Reddit (post + comments), Twitter/X (tweet + metrics + media), Hacker News (post + comments), Stack Overflow (question + answers with code blocks), YouTube (metadata + transcript). For any other URL (news articles, blogs, documentation, etc.), extracts the page title, metadata, and main readable text using lightweight HTML parsing — no headless browser needed.\n  - url (required): Any URL. Supported platforms are auto-detected: GitHub (URL or owner/repo), Reddit, Twitter/X, Hacker News, Stack Overflow, YouTube. All other URLs use generic article extraction.\n  - commentLimit: Max comments to fetch (Reddit default: 20, HN default: 25)\n  - answerLimit: Max answers to fetch for Stack Overflow (default: 5, max: 10)\n  - readme: Include repository README for GitHub (default: true)\n  - languages: Include language breakdown for GitHub (default: true)\n  - transcript: Include video transcript for YouTube (default: true)\n  - lang: Preferred transcript language for YouTube (default: 'en')\n  - maxChars: Max characters of extracted text for generic pages (default: 15000)\n\n### calculate_precise\nPerform highly precise mathematical calculations using bignumber.js. Supports arbitrary-precision arithmetic. Passed numbers should be strings to prevent precision loss. For sqrt, 'b' is ignored.\n  - operation (required): The mathematical operation to perform\n  - a (required): The first operand (must be a valid numeric string)\n  - b: The second operand (must be a valid numeric string). Optional for sqrt.\n\n### execute_javascript\nExecute JavaScript code in a sandboxed Node.js vm context. Much faster than Python for quick data transforms, JSON manipulation, regex, and math. Has access to JSON, Math, Date, RegExp, Array, Object, Map, Set, typed arrays, TextEncoder/TextDecoder, console.log, and all core JS builtins. No access to require, import, process, fetch, setTimeout, filesystem, or network. Use logger.info() to produce output. Returns both captured output and the expression result.\n  - code (required): JavaScript source code to execute. Use logger.info() to produce output. The last expression value is returned as 'result'. Full standard JS built-ins available (JSON, Math, Date, RegExp, Array methods, Map, Set, etc.). No require/import/fetch/process/setTimeout.\n  - timeout: Execution timeout in milliseconds (min 100, max 30000, default 5000).\n\n### search_web\nSearch the web using Brave Search (primary, whole-web) with Google Custom Search fallback. Returns results with titles, URLs, and snippets. Use this for researching topics, finding documentation, looking up current information, or verifying facts. Supports date filtering and site-specific search.\n  - query (required): The search query.\n  - limit: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5, max: 10).\n  - dateRestrict: Restrict results by age. Examples: 'd7' (past 7 days), 'w2' (past 2 weeks), 'm1' (past month), 'y1' (past year).\n  - siteSearch: Restrict search to a specific domain (e.g. 'stackoverflow.com', 'developer.mozilla.org').\n\n### create_task\nCreate a persistent task to track a work item across agentic iterations. Tasks survive context window truncation and memory consolidation, providing reliable Working Memory for complex multi-step workflows. Use this when starting a complex task to maintain a checklist of sub-goals, track progress on multi-file refactors, or record items that must not be forgotten if context is lost. Returns the created task with a unique numeric ID.\n  - subject (required): A brief title for the task (e.g. 'Migrate auth middleware to JWT').\n  - description (required): Detailed description of what needs to be done.\n  - status: Initial status (default: 'pending').\n  - activeForm: Present continuous form shown as spinner text when in_progress (e.g. 'Running tests', 'Refactoring auth module').\n  - metadata: Optional arbitrary key-value metadata to attach to the task.\n\n### list_tasks\nList all tasks for a project, optionally filtered by status. Returns tasks sorted by ID with a summary showing counts per status (pending, in_progress, completed). Use this at the start of a new agentic session to recall what was previously in progress, or after completing a batch of work to audit remaining items.\n  - status: Optional filter — only return tasks with this status.\n  - limit: Maximum number of tasks to return (default: 50, max: 200).\n\n### get_task\nGet a single task by its numeric ID. Returns the full task document including subject, description, status, metadata, and timestamps. Use this to check the current state of a specific task before updating it, or to retrieve detailed metadata attached to a task.\n  - taskId (required): The numeric ID of the task to retrieve.\n\n### update_task\nUpdate an existing task's status, subject, description, or metadata. Use this to mark tasks as 'in_progress' when you start working on them, 'completed' when done, or to refine the description as your understanding of the task evolves. Metadata is merged (not replaced) — you can incrementally add key-value pairs without losing existing metadata.\n  - taskId (required): The numeric ID of the task to update.\n  - status: New status for the task. Setting 'deleted' removes the task entirely.\n  - subject: Updated title for the task.\n  - description: Updated description of what needs to be done.\n  - activeForm: Present continuous form shown as spinner text when in_progress (e.g. 'Running tests', 'Migrating schemas').\n  - metadata: Key-value pairs to merge into existing task metadata.\n\n### upsert_memory\nPersist a piece of information to long-term agent memory. Call this tool in TWO cases:\n1. **Explicit requests**: The user says 'remember', 'save', 'note', 'store', 'keep in mind', or 'don't forget'.\n2. **Implicit preference signals**: The user reveals a personal preference, opinion, or fact about themselves — even without asking you to remember it. Trigger words/patterns include: 'I like ...', 'I love ...', 'I hate ...', 'I dislike ...', 'I prefer ...', 'I enjoy ...', 'I can\\'t stand ...', 'I always ...', 'I never ...', 'my favorite ...', 'I\\'m allergic to ...', 'I\\'m a ... person', or any statement expressing a personal taste, habit, identity trait, or strong opinion. When in doubt, SAVE IT — over-remembering is better than forgetting.\n\nMemories are deduplicated automatically — calling this with content that already exists is safe and will not create duplicates. Returns the stored memory document or null if a near-duplicate was detected.\n  - content (required): The memory content to persist. Should be a clear, self-contained statement (e.g. 'User prefers tabs over spaces' or 'The auth service uses JWT with RS256').\n  - type: Memory category. 'user' for personal preferences, 'feedback' for corrections/style guidance, 'project' for codebase conventions, 'reference' for technical facts. Defaults to 'project'.\n  - title: Optional short label for the memory (e.g. 'Indentation preference'). Improves discoverability during semantic search.\n\n### search_tools\nSearch for available tools by keyword, domain, or label. Returns matching tool names, descriptions, and schemas. Use this to discover what capabilities are available when you need a tool you haven't used before, or to find domain-specific tools (e.g. weather, finance, health). This is a read-only discovery tool — it does not execute anything.\n  - query: Search keyword(s) to match against tool names and descriptions. Example: 'weather', 'file read', 'stock price', 'image generation'.\n  - domain: Filter by tool domain. Known domains include: 'Weather & Environment', 'Finance & Markets', 'Health & Nutrition', 'Knowledge & Reference', 'Workspace', 'Web', 'Browser', 'Task Management', 'Communication', 'Creative', etc.\n  - label: Filter by label category (e.g. 'coding', 'web', 'smart_home').\n  - limit: Maximum results to return (1–50). Default: 20.\n\n### think\nUse this tool to reason through complex problems step-by-step before acting. Write your private reasoning, analysis, or plan here — this content is NOT shown to the user. Use this when you need to: break down a multi-step task, weigh trade-offs between approaches, analyze information from previous tool calls, plan your next actions, or reason about ambiguous requirements. This tool does not execute anything — it simply records your thinking for context continuity.\n  - thought (required): Your private reasoning, analysis, or plan. Be thorough — this is your scratchpad.\n\n### sleep\nPause execution for a specified duration. Use for polling workflows — e.g. wait for a build to finish, a server to restart, or a deployment to propagate before checking results. Maximum duration is 120 seconds. The pause can be cancelled if the user aborts the session.\n  - duration_seconds (required): How long to wait in seconds (1–120). Default: 5.\n  - reason: Brief explanation of why you are waiting (shown to the user).\n\n### synthetic_output\nProduce a structured JSON output conforming to a defined schema. Use this when the user or a downstream system needs machine-readable data rather than natural language. Provide the output format as a JSON Schema object and the data that conforms to it. The tool validates the data against the schema and returns the validated result. Use cases: API-like responses, data extraction, typed reports, pipeline outputs.\n  - schema: JSON Schema definition for the expected output structure. Example: { type: 'object', properties: { title: { type: 'string' }, score: { type: 'number' } }, required: ['title'] }.\n  - data (required): The structured data to output. Must conform to the provided schema. Example: { title: 'My Report', score: 95 }.\n  - label: Optional label for this output (e.g. 'analysis_result', 'extracted_entities').\n\n### enter_plan_mode\nSwitch into planning mode. While in plan mode, you will not have access to any tools — you can only output text. Use this to produce a structured implementation plan before executing changes. Call exit_plan_mode when you are ready to resume tool execution. Use this when the task is complex and benefits from upfront planning.\n  - reason: Why you are entering plan mode (shown to the user).\n\n### exit_plan_mode\nExit planning mode and resume normal tool execution. Call this after you have produced your plan and are ready to execute it with tools.\n  - summary: Brief summary of the plan you are about to execute.\n\n### create_skill\nCreate a reusable workflow skill. Skills are stored prompt templates with variable interpolation ({{variable}}) that can be invoked by name. Use this to capture multi-step workflows (refactor→test→commit, analyze→report, etc.) as reusable atomic operations. Skills persist across sessions and can be shared across agents.\n  - name (required): Unique skill name (e.g. 'refactor_and_test', 'code_review'). Used as the skill ID.\n  - description: What the skill does — shown when listing skills.\n  - prompt (required): The prompt template to execute. Use {{variable}} syntax for parameters.\n  - steps: Optional: ordered list of step descriptions for documentation.\n  - tools: Optional: specific tools to enable. If omitted, all tools are available.\n  - maxIterations: Optional: max agentic loop iterations for the skill run (1-100). Default: 25.\n  - model: Optional: model override for the skill run.\n\n### execute_skill\nExecute a previously created skill by its ID. The skill's prompt template is interpolated with the provided variables and executed as an inline agentic task. Use list_skills to see available skills.\n  - skillId (required): The skill ID to execute (derived from the skill name).\n  - variables: Key-value pairs for {{variable}} interpolation in the skill's prompt template.\n\n### list_skills\nList all available skills. Skills are reusable workflow templates created with create_skill.\n  - project: Optional: filter by project scope.\n\n### delete_skill\nDelete a skill by its ID.\n  - skillId (required): The skill ID to delete.\n\n### enter_worktree\nEnter an isolated git worktree for the current conversation. Creates a new branch and redirects all file/git/shell tool calls to the worktree directory. Use this to try risky refactors, experimental changes, or speculative edits without affecting the main branch. Your full conversation context is preserved. Call exit_worktree to merge or discard when done.\n  - reason: Why you're entering an isolated worktree (e.g. 'risky refactor', 'experimental approach').\n\n### exit_worktree\nExit the current isolated worktree and return to the main workspace. Choose to 'merge' changes back to the main branch or 'discard' them entirely. If merging, changes are committed and merged automatically.\n  - action (required): 'merge' to apply changes to main branch, 'discard' to throw them away.\n  - commitMessage: Commit message for the merge (used when action is 'merge'). Auto-generated if not provided.\n\n### write_todo\nWrite or update a persistent TODO checklist for the current project. Maintains a structured list of items with completion status. Use this to track multi-step work, record progress, and keep a living checklist that persists across conversation turns. Each item has a status: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'. Call with the full updated list — it replaces the previous state.\n  - items (required): Full list of todo items. Replaces the previous list entirely.\n\n### brief\nProduce a compressed summary of the current conversation context. Use this tool when the conversation is getting long and you need to consolidate your understanding before continuing. The summary you write is stored and can be referenced in future turns to recover context. This is NOT shown to the user — it is your private working memory.\n  - summary (required): Your compressed summary of the conversation so far. Include: key decisions made, files modified, current task state, and what remains to be done.\n  - keyFiles: Optional: list of key file paths relevant to the current work.\n  - openQuestions: Optional: unresolved questions or ambiguities.\n\n### ask_user_question\nAsk the user one or more questions and wait for their responses before continuing. Use this when you need clarification, a decision between options, or explicit confirmation before proceeding with a potentially impactful action. The agent loop pauses until the user responds. You can batch up to 4 related questions in a single call to reduce round-trips.\n  - question: The question to present to the user. For a single question, use this directly. For multiple questions, use the 'questions' array instead.\n  - choices: Optional: predefined answer choices for a single question.\n  - context: Optional: additional context shown below a single question.\n  - questions: Optional: batch multiple related questions in one call (up to 4). Each item is a question object.\n\n### set_timer\nSet a one-shot timer or a recurring cron within this conversation that fires an instruction or prompt back into this conversation after a duration. Use this to wait, sleep, yield, defer execution, or to schedule periodic background checks on long-running tasks or builds.\n  - prompt (required): The prompt text or instruction to execute when the timer expires.\n  - durationSeconds: Optional: Number of seconds to wait before firing (one-shot, e.g., 10). Maximum: 86400 (24 hours).\n  - cronExpression: Optional: A standard 5-field cron expression for recurring runs (e.g. '*/5 * * * *').\n  - maxIterations: Optional: Maximum iterations/repeats for recurring timers before automatically expiring.\n\n### list_timers\nList all active timers and recurring cron schedules for the current conversation.\n\n\n### cancel_timer\nCancel an active timer or recurring cron in the current conversation.\n  - timerId (required): The unique ID of the timer or schedule to cancel.\n\n### create_team\nSpawn one or more worker agents that execute in parallel, each in an isolated git worktree. Workers have access to the full tool suite (read, write, search, shell). Use for parallelizable research, implementation, or verification tasks. For a single task, provide one member. For parallel work, provide up to 10 members in a single call. Returns results from all members when they all complete.\n  - name (required): Team name for identification (e.g. 'auth_refactor', 'research').\n  - members (required): Array of worker definitions (max 10). Each member runs autonomously in its own worktree.\n\n### send_message\nSend a follow-up message to a running or completed worker agent. Use to continue work, provide corrections, or give new instructions.\n  - to (required): Agent ID returned by create_team\n  - message (required): Follow-up instructions for the worker\n\n### stop_agent\nStop a running worker agent. The worker's worktree is cleaned up.\n  - agent_id (required): Agent ID to stop\n\n### get_task_output\nRead the output from a previously spawned worker agent by its agent ID. Use this to check on a worker's result after it has completed, or to read partial output from a still-running worker. Returns the worker's final text, tool usage stats, diff summary, and status.\n  - agent_id (required): The agent ID returned by create_team.\n\n### delete_team\nStop and remove all workers in a named team. Cleans up worktrees for all members.\n  - teamName (required): The team name to delete (as provided to create_team).\n\n**Compute**\n### create_3d_mesh\nCreate a 3D object from raw triangle mesh data — vertices and face indices. IMPORTANT: You can build the 3D mesh incrementally — break the generation into logical parts (e.g. base, wings, details, sections) and call this tool multiple times using the sessionId returned from the first call. Pass the sessionId to append new vertices and faces. Note: Face indices in subsequent calls are absolute (0-based indexing relative to the total accumulated vertices). Between calls, briefly describe what you just added and what comes next so the user can follow along. Omit sessionId to start a new 3D mesh session. The response contains a sceneEmbedUrl — render it with ![3D Mesh](sceneEmbedUrl) markdown so the user sees the interactive 3D scene inline. Max 50,000 total vertices and 100,000 total faces per session.\n  - sessionId: Optional session ID returned from a prior create_3d_mesh call. Pass this to append new vertices and faces to an existing mesh. Omit to start a new 3D mesh session.\n  - vertices (required): Array of vertex positions. Each vertex is [x, y, z]. Example: [[0,1,0], [1,-1,0], [-1,-1,0]]\n  - faces (required): Array of triangle face indices. Each face is [v0, v1, v2] referencing vertex indices. Example: [[0,1,2]]\n  - normals: Optional per-vertex normals [nx, ny, nz]. Must match vertex count. Omit to auto-compute.\n  - colors: Optional per-vertex colors as CSS color strings. Must match vertex count. Example: ['#ff6347', '#38bdf8', '#4ade80']\n  - options: Rendering options\n\n### create_3d_model\nCreate a 3D object/model by composing primitive shapes with PBR materials and transforms. Available shapes: box, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus, torusKnot, plane, ring, circle, dodecahedron, icosahedron, octahedron, tetrahedron, capsule. Each object supports position, rotation (degrees), scale, and material properties (color, metalness, roughness, opacity, emissive, wireframe, flatShading). Use cases: architectural mockups, abstract sculptures, game prototyping, educational geometry, product showcases. The response contains a sceneEmbedUrl — render it with ![3D Model](sceneEmbedUrl) markdown so the user sees the interactive 3D model inline. Max 200 objects per call. Supports shadow casting, ambient/directional lighting control, and auto-orbit camera. When the user attaches an image, set textureUrl to 'reference' on the specific objects that should display it — the system will replace 'reference' with the actual image data automatically. Only mark objects that should show the user's image; leave textureUrl unset on objects that should use solid material colors. Do NOT search the web for image URLs. Supports progressive, step-by-step incremental building using a sessionId (analogous to the draw_turtle graphics tool) where subsequent calls with the same sessionId append new objects to the existing model rather than overwriting it.\n  - sessionId: Optional session ID returned from a previous create_3d_model call. Pass this to append new objects to an existing 3D model progressively. Omit to start a new 3D model session.\n  - objects (required): Array of primitive shape objects to compose into a 3D model.\n  - options: Model rendering options\n\n### create_3d_scene\nCreate a rich 3D scene using a declarative scene graph with hierarchical grouping, built-in animations, environment lighting presets, ground planes, and 3D text labels. This is the highest-level 3D tool. Object types: box, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus, torusKnot, plane, ring, circle, dodecahedron, icosahedron, octahedron, tetrahedron, capsule, group (container for children), text3d (3D text label). Built-in animations: spin, bounce, orbit, pulse, float — applied per-object with configurable speed/amplitude. Environment presets: studio, outdoor, night, sunset, dawn, warehouse, neutral — control ambient, directional, fill, and hemisphere lighting automatically. Supports ground plane with shadows, fog, camera FOV control, and auto-orbit. Use cases: product showcases, animated explainers, data visualization, artistic compositions, holiday scenes. The response contains a sceneEmbedUrl — render it with ![3D Scene](sceneEmbedUrl) markdown so the user sees the interactive 3D scene inline. Max 300 total objects (including nested children), max 5 levels of nesting. When the user attaches an image, set textureUrl to 'reference' on the specific objects that should display it — the system will replace 'reference' with the actual image data automatically. Only mark objects that should show the user's image; leave textureUrl unset on objects that should use solid material colors. Do NOT search the web for image URLs. Supports progressive, step-by-step incremental building using a sessionId (analogous to the draw_turtle graphics tool) where subsequent calls with the same sessionId append new objects to the existing scene rather than overwriting it.\n  - sessionId: Optional session ID returned from a previous create_3d_scene call. Pass this to append new objects to an existing 3D scene progressively. Omit to start a new 3D scene session.\n  - scene: Scene-level configuration: environment, background, ground, camera, fog.\n  - objects (required): Array of scene objects. Each can be a shape, a group (with children), or text3d.\n  - options: Scene rendering options\n\n## Coding Guidelines\n- Always read relevant files before making edits to understand context\n- Use str_replace_file for targeted edits — it's safer and preserves unchanged content. Reserve write_file for creating new files or full rewrites only\n- Use patch_file for multi-hunk edits across non-adjacent sections of the same file\n- After making changes, verify them by reading the modified section\n- Keep your explanations concise and technical\n\n## Environment\n- OS: Linux (WSL2)\n- Workspace: /workspace"
